newsitem.title: USA: Arraignment of former ADM executives set.
newsitem.headline: Arraignment of former ADM executives set.

text.p: The arraignment of three former Archer Daniels Midland Co. executives facing price-fixing charges was postponed until Thursday, a federal prosecutor said Monday.

Randall Sanborn of the U.S. Attorney's office in Chicago said the arraignment, originally set for Monday, was moved after prosecutors failed to get the case assigned to the judge who presided over ADM's antitrust case, in which the company pleaded guilty to two counts of price-fixing and agreed to pay a record $100 million fine.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Scott Lassar said U.S. District Judge Blanche Manning will preside over the case against Michael Andreas, who recently took leave as vice chairman of ADM; Terrance Wilson, a former group vice president in charge of corn refining; and Mark Whitacre, who had headed ADM's BioProducts Division.
The three were charged with allegedly fixing prices of lysine, a feed additive.

The case was assigned originally to Manning, but prosecutors had attempted to have it transferred to Judge Ruben Castillo, who heard Decatur, Ill.-based ADM's antitrust case, in which it pleaded guilty to fixing prices of lysine and citric acid, a food additive, and agreed to pay the fine, the biggest ever in an antitrust case.
Michael Andreas is the son of ADM Chairman Dwayne Andreas.
Whitacre acted as an informant for more than three years as part of the Justice Department's investigation of alleged price-fixing in the feed and food additives industries.
He was fired from Decatur, Ill.-based ADM in August 1995 after the company alleged he stole $9 million. Whitacre has denied those charges.
Earlier this month, Whitacre said he was no longer cooperating with the government in its price-fixing case.
